## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sirimāvimānavatthu* (Vv 16) is a canonical verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The narrative concerns Sirimā, described in the tradition as a wife of King Bimbisāra who, after passing away and being reborn as a *devī* in a celestial mansion, proclaims her unshakable faith and confidence in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records six modern translations of the text in six languages [SuttaCentral].
No curated cross-canonical parallels are recorded for the text on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal correspondence with the commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which shares 20 passages (comprising 2,386 characters; notably segments 10.3–13.4 matching segments 696–706_0) [DharmaNexus]. In other Buddhist languages, DharmaNexus detects automated alignments with the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu-avadāna* (5 matches, highest plausibility score 75, e.g. §3.2), as well as lower-scoring matches with the Tibetan versions of the *Abhiniṣkramaṇa-sūtra* (D0301) and the *Lalitavistara* (D0095), and the Chinese *Fo shuo geigu zhangzhe nü dedu yinyuan jing* (Taishō 130) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
